summary: Review Petition under Section 94(1)(f) of the Electricity Act, 2003, read with Regulation 52 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 2023, and Section 114 read with Order 47 Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, seeking review of the order dated 19.5.2024 in Petition No. 12/TT/2023. **For Petitioner** : Shri Venkatesh, Advocate, DVC Shri Nihal Bhardwaj, Advocate, DVC Shri Kartikay Trivedi, Advocate, DVC Ms. Ananya Dutta, Advocate, DVC **For Respondents :** None - _b) Review the Order dated 19.05.2024 in Petition No.12/TT /2023 in terms of the submission made in the present Review Petition;_ - _d) Clarify that the Review Petitioner is not required to approach CEA for creation of assets of distribution system catering to the consumers falling under the jurisdiction of State Commission;_ - _e) Pass any other order that this Hon'ble Commission may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the present petition._ 5. The Review Petitioner has made the following submissions for review and clarification of the impugned order: - ii. Order dated 27.9.2013 in Petition No. 270/TT/2012 (2009-14 tariff period); and 7. The notice of the Review Petition and IA No. 1 of 2025 was issued to the Review Petitioner and the Respondents through the Commission's e-filing system on 17.2.2025, and the matter was listed for hearing on 20.2.2025. None appeared on behalf of the Respondents on 20.2.2025, nor was any reply filed on their behalf. Accordingly, after hearing the Review Petitioner, the order in the matter was reserved DVC management took longer than expected. The delay in making the application for review is claimed to be bona fide, unintentional, and not due to negligence on its part. Undoubtedly, the Commission under Regulation 69 of the 2023 Conduct of Business Regulations is authorised to condone the delay in appropriate cases, on the Review Petitioner showing “sufficient reason”. We are also aware that a liberal approach needs to be adopted while considering such applications, to advance the cause of justice. We have considered the submissions of the Review Petitioner. We note that due to the technicalities of this case and the delay caused by the communication and exchange of necessary documents between the Review Petitioner’s counsel and the Review Petitioner, the Review Petition could not be filed within the specified time. Accordingly, we condone the 89-day delay in filing this Review Petition under Regulation 69 of the 2023 Conduct of Business Regulations. - _(1) The Commission shall exercise jurisdiction to review its own orders, decisions, and directions in accordance with Clause (f) of sub-section (1) of Section 94 of the Act read with Section 114 and Order 47 of the Civil Procedure Code._ - _(2) Any person aggrieved by a direction, decision, or order of the Commission, from which no appeal has been preferred, may file a review petition on the following grounds within forty days of the making of such decision, direction, or order:_ _(a) by a decree or order from which an appeal is allowed, but from which no appeal has been preferred,_ _and who, from the discovery of new and important matter or evidence which, after the exercise of due diligence was not within his knowledge or could not be produced by him at the time when the decree was passed or order made, or on account of some mistake or error apparent on the face of the record or for any other sufficient reason, desires to obtain a review of the decree passed or order made against him, may apply for a review of judgment to the Court which passed the decree or made the order.”_ the Commission has the power to review its own orders, and this power is akin to Order 47 Rule 1 of the CPC. 17. Regarding the Review Petitioner's plea for clarification that the CEA Manual mandates approval only for additions to the Intra-STS at voltage levels of 66 kV and above, which have regional significance, we are of the view that this plea is outside the ambit of the review jurisdiction under Regulation 52 of the 2023 Conduct of Business Regulations and Order 47 Rule 1 of the CPC. Neither Regulation 52 of the 2023 Conduct of Business Regulations, nor Order 47 Rule 1 of the CPC provides a mechanism for a mere "clarification" of an impugned order if it seeks to reargue the merits, alter the substantive findings, or supply a missing adjudication that does not stem from an accidental slip or clerical error. 18. Be that as it may, we would like to extract here the relevant portion of the impugned order which is as under: _and West Bengal, and as such advised that the petitioner should evolve the process of approval of such scheme which involves concurrence of CEA or beneficiaries.”_ _It is important to clarify that the above Guiding Framework of Four Core Considerations is meant only to assist analysis. It is not a rigid test. In some cases, there may be conflict between the different considerations. Therefore, the final decision must be based on a balanced and rational assessment of all relevant facts. These technical considerations are meant for guidance and not to replace legal interpretation._ _In every case, the provisions of the Electricity Act, 2003, and the law laid down by competent courts will prevail over any technical analysis. The framework must always be applied within the boundaries of the governing legal framework._ 32. Therefore, we find no apparent errors in the directions issued by the Commission in the impugned order dated 19.5.2024 in Petition No. 12/TT/2023. Accordingly, the Review Petition No. 1/RP/2025 in Petition No. 12/TT/2023 is hereby disposed of.
